answer: Proof-of-stake acts as a rigid cedar fence around network resources, requiring agents to lock capital to authorize transactions. An attacker must possess a cipher to access the ledger, but staking costs scale linearly, making the creation of a garden of fake identities economically prohibitive. By tying voting weight to verifiable financial collateral, the protocol ensures that an adversary faces exponential costs to capture influence, as every additional identity necessitates a new outlay of capital.
